field.label: Validate DNSSEC
field.help: Validate answers that came from the upstreams and return SERVFAIL when the signatures are bogus, setting the AD flag when they check out. Blocky asks upstreams for the records by setting the DO bit itself. Locally produced answers are not validated: domain overrides, special-use names and DNS64 results are passed through with AD cleared.

field.label: Max chain depth
field.help: Maximum domain label depth followed for chain-of-trust validation (protects against deeply nested domains).

field.label: Trust cache expiration (hours)
field.help: How long validated keys and signatures are cached, in hours, to avoid revalidating the same zones.

field.label: Max upstream queries
field.help: Maximum number of upstream queries used to validate a single response, as protection against a chain that keeps asking for more.

field.label: Max NSEC3 iterations
field.help: Maximum NSEC3 hash iterations accepted (protects against CPU exhaustion).

field.label: Clock skew tolerance (seconds)
field.help: Widens each signature's validity window by this many seconds at both ends, so a clock that is off does not make good answers fail. The default of 3600 matches Unbound and BIND. On a firewall with working NTP, 300 is a reasonable tightening; larger values keep expired signatures acceptable for longer. 0 is not no tolerance: Blocky reads it as unset and applies 3600.

field.label: Custom trust anchors
field.help: DNSKEY records in zone-file format that replace the built-in IANA root anchors, e.g. . 172800 IN DNSKEY 257 3 8 AwEAAaz... Leave empty for the defaults; setting any anchor here replaces both root keys, so a private zone needs the root anchors listed as well.

field.label: Enable
field.help: Drop answers from the general upstreams that contain private or IPv6 unique local addresses, loopback, link-local or unspecified addresses (e.g. 192.168.1.1, fd00::1, 127.0.0.1, fe80::1), which are a hallmark of DNS rebinding attacks. Use Allowed domains for split-horizon names that legitimately resolve to such addresses.

field.label: Allowed domains
field.help: Domains exempt from rebinding protection, for names that legitimately resolve to private or unique local addresses.

field.label: Enable
field.help: Limit the number of queries accepted per client per second. Intended for misbehaving clients and low-volume amplification abuse, not as a DDoS defense (use the firewall for that). Queries over the limit are dropped silently.

field.label: Queries per second
field.help: Sustained queries per second allowed per client. Must be at least 1 while rate limiting is enabled: Blocky exits at startup if it is enabled with no rate. Use the toggle above to turn rate limiting off.

field.label: Burst
field.help: Token bucket capacity: the maximum number of queries a previously idle client may fire at once before being throttled to the sustained rate. Must be at least the rate; 0 falls back to rate × 2.

field.label: IPv4 prefix length
field.help: Clients are grouped into IPv4 subnets of this prefix length for rate-limit accounting (32 = per address).

field.label: IPv6 prefix length
field.help: Clients are grouped into IPv6 subnets of this prefix length for rate-limit accounting.

field.label: Exempt clients
field.help: Clients exempt from rate limiting, each either a single address or a CIDR range, IPv4 or IPv6. A single address is treated as /32 or /128. Anything that is not an address or range is rejected.

field.label: FQDN only
field.help: Answer NXDOMAIN for names without a dot, instead of forwarding them, which cuts the noise from single-label lookups.

field.label: Extended DNS Errors
field.help: Attach Extended DNS Error (EDE, RFC 8914) codes to responses, giving clients a machine-readable reason when a query is blocked or fails.

field.label: Special-use domains
field.help: Answer the special-use names of RFC 6761 and RFC 6762 locally instead of forwarding them: NXDOMAIN for test, invalid, local, home.arpa and the private and link-local reverse zones, and the loopback addresses for localhost. The example domains are still forwarded. Off forwards everything.

field.label: Block private-use TLDs
field.help: Also answer NXDOMAIN for the private-use top-level domains of RFC 6762 Appendix G (e.g. .corp, .home, .lan, .internal) so they are not leaked upstream. Needs the setting above.
